messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: reverting to Stan 1.3 [running multiple versions of RStan in R]
parts:
The easiest way to do it is to install 1.3 to a different directory. By default, it will install to the first directory given by

.libPaths()

which for me is

[1] "/opt/site-library"             "/usr/local/lib/R/site-library" "/usr/lib/R/site-library"      
[4] "/usr/lib/R/library"          

install_url('https://github.com/stan-dev/rstan/releases/download/v1.3.0/rstan_1.3.0.tar.gz', args = paste0("--library=", .libPaths()[2]))
Downloading rstan_1.3.0.tar.gz from https://github.com/stan-dev/rstan/releases/download/v1.3.0/rstan_1.3.0.tar.gz
Installing package from /tmp/RtmpJLwfA3/rstan_1.3.0.tar.gz
Installing rstan

You just need to make sure that you have write permissions for the folder you are trying to install to. Then to use v1.3.0 instead of v2.0.0, you can do

library(rstan, lib.loc = .libPaths()[2])

or wherever you installed v1.3.0. It won't work to have two versions of rstan loaded at the same time, nor will it work on Windows to detach() one version and load the other in the same R session. You have to restart R.

Ben

parts:
On Sat, Oct 19, 2013 at 01:05:19PM -0400, Bob Carpenter wrote:
> If I understood Jiqiang's earlier e-mail when we were
> working on distribution, R only allows a single version
> of a package to be installed.
>
> I suppose one way to get around this would be to rename
> one of the packages at the source level, but I don't know how
> to do that.
>
> - Bob
>
> On 10/19/13 4:46 AM, Janne Sinkkonen wrote:
>> Is there an easy or semi-easy way to have multiple stan and rstan installations in a single R?

Install the different versions to 2 different R library directories, and then do, e.g.,
library("rstan", lib.loc="mydirFor1.3")

Attempting to use both libraries in the same R session might be
hazardous, though maybe if you unload the library you'll be able to.
But using them in 2 different R sessions should work fine.

No need to alter the source.

Ross Boylan
